t: The poop deck mooring area was poorly cleaned, with patches of funnel soot left on deck.
f: Include deck cleanliness in routine rounds and clear soot deposits promptly, especially in mooring areas.

t: A securing clip on a work vest used for overside work while rigging pilot and accommodation ladders was broken.
f: Inspect overside work vests before each use and replace damaged clips or buckles.

t: The crew member responsible had not spotted the broken clip on one of the two work vests kept for rigging pilot/accommodation ladders.
f: Check PPE item by item during safety rounds, not with a quick glance at the locker.

t: Interviewee did not know the portable gas detectors used for entry permits could not sample the full depth of the cargo tanks and pump room.
f: Know your gas detector's sampling hose limits and confirm they reach the bottom of each space before entry.

t: No working-aloft permits were raised for the quarterly water mist nozzle test, which needed collection baskets rigged 4-6 m above deck.
f: Raise a working-aloft permit for any test or maintenance job above the company's height threshold.

t: Per the maker's manual, the three portable gas detectors could only sample to 50 ft, while the cargo tanks and pump room were about 20 m deep.
f: Match sampling hose length and pump capacity to the deepest space on board and order extensions if needed.

t: Same issue recorded again: entry-permit gas detectors had a 50 ft sampling limit against cargo tank and pump room depths of about 20 m.
f: Verify detector capability against space depth whenever gas testing equipment or permits are reviewed.

t: The monthly safety inspection had missed mould covering about half of the forecastle store ceiling.
f: Look up as well as around during monthly inspections and report damp or mould for cleaning and ventilation.

t: Interviewee was not familiar with where the ship's fire doors were, what they were for or how they operated.
f: Walk the fire control plan and be ready to explain fire door types, locations and how they close.

t: Pyrotechnics on the bridge and in both lifeboats were not stowed in watertight containers; corrected before the inspector left.
f: Keep all pyrotechnics in approved watertight containers and check this during LSA inspections.

t: Interviewee admitted not noticing that the bridge and lifeboat pyrotechnics were outside approved watertight containers.
f: Add 'pyrotechnics in watertight container' as a specific line on the LSA inspection checklist.

t: Lube oil was leaking from connections under the LO cooler, with a small container placed to catch it instead of a repair; fixed during inspection.
f: Repair leaks at the source and raise a defect; a drip tin is not a fix.

t: The person responsible for machinery space safety inspections had not recorded the lube oil cooler leak.
f: Record every leak found on rounds and follow it through to repair.

t: Four forecastle light fittings each had one of two tubes burnt out, including an emergency light at the entrance.
f: Replace failed lamps promptly and test emergency lighting during routine checks.

t: The officer in charge of forecastle safety inspections admitted missing the four defective light fittings.
f: Switch on and check all lighting, including emergency lights, during forecastle inspections.

t: The company procedure for the Coating Technical File did not list its required contents (yard coating records, specs, inspection, repairs); these sat in a dry-dock folder.
f: Know what the Coating Technical File must contain and keep coating records in that file.

t: Company procedures gave no clear guidance on cross-track distance for different passage stages (as NP232 suggests), though the plan had XTD for each leg.
f: Be ready to explain how the XTD for each leg (pilotage, coastal, open sea) was chosen.

t: The procedure for MARPOL Annex VI (NOx) record books did not say what to record, who records, how to make late entries or corrections, or when the Master signs.
f: Know who keeps each Annex VI record book, how late entries and corrections are made and when the Master signs.

t: Sea anchor ropes and other gear inside the free-fall lifeboat were left unlashed and could shift during launch.
f: After any lifeboat maintenance, re-secure all loose equipment before leaving the boat.

t: Interviewee said the free-fall lifeboat equipment had not been re-lashed after routine maintenance.
f: Make 're-stow and lash all items' the final step of every lifeboat maintenance job.

t: Same finding recorded as a learning gap: lifeboat equipment was left unsecured after routine maintenance work.
f: Use a close-out check after lifeboat work so a second person confirms all gear is secured.

t: The stern light on the poop deck had a cracked lamp base; it had been reported through the defect system.
f: Check navigation lights and fittings daily and keep spares to repair defects quickly.

t: A rubber step near the bottom of the port pilot ladder in use was deformed; the ladder was replaced during the inspection.
f: Inspect every step of the pilot ladder before rigging and replace ladders with damaged steps.

t: Interviewee said the deformed pilot ladder step had been missed during the safety inspection through oversight.
f: Inspect pilot ladders step by step, not just a glance at the rolled-up ladder.

t: No hard copy of the cyber contingency plan was on board, only a soft copy; it was printed once pointed out.
f: Keep printed copies of cyber contingency plans, as IT systems may be down when you need them.

t: A locking nut on the brake tightening screw was being used as a stopper to set the mooring winch brake torque.
f: Set winch brakes as per the brake test results and maker's guidance, and know how the setting is marked.

t: The accompanying deck officer was not fully familiar with how mooring winch brake rendering indications are set.
f: Know your winch brake rendering marks, how they were set after brake testing and how to use them.

t: Also recorded as a learning gap: the deck officer could not fully explain the setting of winch brake rendering marks.
f: Include winch brake setting and rendering marks in mooring familiarisation and toolbox talks.

t: Photo not representative: the mooring winch brake rendering marks and arrow indicators were found ineffective on board.
f: Keep winch brake marks clearly painted and make sure uploaded photos reflect current condition.

t: The photo uploaded to the OCIMF repository did not give a clear view of the main engine.
f: Review photo uploads against each required view before submitting and retake unclear images.

t: The familiarisation checklist did not cover job-specific tasks and equipment for galley and catering staff.
f: Make sure catering staff get documented familiarisation on galley equipment and its hazards.

t: Interviewee did not understand the mooring winch brakes and could not say why brakes are tightened only to the rendering point setting.
f: Understand why brakes are set to render at a set load: the line should slip before it parts.

t: The ballast water treatment system was out of service with its electro-chlorination unit dismantled; logged and acknowledged by shore months earlier.
f: Track long-standing defects with the office and know the contingency measures while the BWTS is down.

t: A CCR table set an initial loading velocity of 1 m/s at the 6 or 8 inch tank inlets but did not give the matching loading rates.
f: Convert inlet velocity limits into m3/h for each inlet size so the initial loading rate is clear.

t: Where the route crossed the safety contour, this was not highlighted in the passage plan; officers said it was only discussed in briefings.
f: Mark any safety contour crossing in the plan and on ECDIS with the precautions to be taken.

t: Two explosion-proof light covers on the main deck were loose with threads exposed, and at least three more were painted over, spoiling the flame path.
f: Never paint flameproof fittings and check their covers are fully tightened during deck rounds.

t: Main deck safety inspections had not picked up the defective explosion-proof light enclosures.
f: Make flameproof fittings (covers, threads, paint) a specific item in deck safety inspections.

t: Interviewee did not understand the ECDIS date-dependent function or how to use it.
f: Practise setting the ECDIS viewing date to check date-dependent chart features for your ETA.

t: Operator procedure required only the BNWAS power failure alarm test, not a check of all three alarm stages on the secondary power supply.
f: When testing power changeover, confirm the BNWAS runs through all alarm stages on secondary supply.

t: The main deck safety inspection checklist did not include checking bonding wires.
f: Add bonding straps on cargo pipelines and hoses to the deck inspection routine.

t: There was no procedure or safety guidance for handling and rigging razor wire.
f: Brief crew on razor wire hazards and PPE and use a risk assessment before rigging it.

t: Interviewee thought the ship's self-buoyant immersion suits had to be worn with a lifejacket, showing unfamiliarity with the type carried.
f: Know whether your immersion suits are buoyant types and whether a lifejacket is needed with them.

t: Interviewee was not aware of the term SIMOPS (simultaneous operations).
f: Know what SIMOPS means and how the company controls simultaneous operations such as bunkering during cargo.

t: There was no ship-specific checklist for inspecting machinery space fire prevention, such as hot surface insulation and flammable liquid leaks.
f: Use a ship-specific checklist covering hot surfaces, lagging and fuel/oil leak sources in the engine room.

t: Rest hour records for one month showed several breaches of the 24-hour minimum for the Master, C/O, 2/O and 3/O.
f: Review rest hours daily and plan work so nobody drops below the minimum; record and address breaches.

t: The magnetic compass bowl had a large air bubble (about 10 x 3 cm); the crew removed it during the inspection.
f: Check the magnetic compass bowl for bubbles during routine bridge checks.

t: The officer doing safety rounds on deck had overlooked the large air bubble in the magnetic compass bowl.
f: Include the standard compass on the monkey island in regular safety rounds.

t: A cargo pump's local hydraulic pressure gauge on deck had no needle.
f: Replace broken gauges promptly using the spares carried.

t: Interviewee knew the gauge needle was missing and a spare gauge was on board, but had not raised a defect report.
f: Raise a defect for every fault you know about, even if a quick fix is planned.

t: The stud in the first link of the port anchor chain had come loose and shifted against the next link.
f: Inspect anchor chain links and studs during anchor inspections and when heaving up.

t: Interviewee admitted missing the loose anchor chain stud during routine inspections, so it was not on the defect list.
f: Look closely at chain studs during anchor inspections and log any defect found.

t: Records showed an eight-month gap between technical superintendent visits, with no other marine or safety superintendent visit in between.
f: Keep superintendent visit reports on board and flag to the office if visits are overdue.

t: A 20 m fire hose was found where the safety plan required a 15 m hose; hoses had been mixed up after pressure testing.
f: After hose testing, return each hose to its listed location with the correct length.

t: A navigation assessment report left the assessor's qualifications and seagoing experience blank.
f: Check navigation assessment reports include the assessor's qualifications and experience before filing.

t: Another navigation assessment report also omitted the assessor's qualifications and experience.
f: Ask the assessor to fill in qualification and experience details before the report is closed.

t: A cargo audit finding (risk assessment reference missing from the cargo plan) was still open past its seven-day close-out deadline.
f: Track internal audit findings to closure within the deadline and update the system.

t: Engineer officers' simulator training certificates did not state the propulsion type covered.
f: Check that engineer simulator certificates state the relevant propulsion type.

t: Interviewee admitted not removing the air bubble from the standard magnetic compass on the monkey island.
f: Check the monkey island compass regularly and remove bubbles using the maker's method.

t: The nitrogen line was pressure tested at 2.4 bar although its working pressure was 0.2 bar and the recommended test pressure 0.24 bar.
f: Confirm the correct test pressure for each line before testing and record it.

t: Interviewee did not know the recommended test pressure for the nitrogen line.
f: Know the working and test pressures of the lines you are responsible for.

t: No photograph had been provided of the double block and bleed arrangement for the nitrogen generator.
f: Check every required photo is uploaded before the inspection.

t: The SMS required an up-to-date certificate index in the statutory certificate files, but none was found in either file.
f: Keep the certificate index current and placed in the certificate files as the SMS requires.

t: A crankcase inspection with web deflections had been carried out, but no enclosed space entry permit was raised for it.
f: Treat crankcase entry as enclosed space entry: ventilate, test the atmosphere and raise a permit.

t: A BWTS filter in the pump room was leaking water continuously.
f: Report and repair BWTS leaks promptly and track them in the defect system.

t: The local differential pressure transmitter on a BWTS filter was blank while the system was running and the CCR showed readings.
f: Compare local BWTS instruments with remote readings and report blank displays.

t: The SMS required an OWS operational check before port arrival, logged in the engine log and ORB, but none was recorded for this port.
f: Follow the pre-arrival OWS test requirement and record it in both the engine log and the ORB.

t: No summary records showed staff progress in the company's behavioural competency assessment programme.
f: Keep a summary of each crew member's behavioural competency assessments on board.

t: Emergency generator fuel injection line connections had no anti-splash tape, missed in routine inspections; fixed during the inspection.
f: Check spray protection on fuel connections near hot surfaces, including on the emergency generator.

t: The switch linking the fire alarm to accommodation ventilation shutdown was left on bypass instead of normal; reset during the inspection.
f: Check fire alarm interlock and bypass switches are in the normal position during safety rounds.

t: The 2/O did not know which sound signal to give to show he was altering course to starboard.
f: Revise COLREG manoeuvring signals: one short blast means 'I am altering my course to starboard'.

t: The first aid kit on the bridge had no eye pad.
f: Check first aid kits against their contents list and restock after use.

t: Pilot ladders in use had certificates more than 30 months old and had not been load tested.
f: Track pilot ladder certificate dates and arrange testing or renewal before limits are reached.

t: The fixed flammable gas detection system for ballast tanks and accommodation entrances was defective; logged, acknowledged by shore and class informed.
f: Know the interim measures, such as portable gas checks, while fixed gas detection is out of service.

t: Two mooring lines in use on the poop deck had torn sections of their polyester jacket over the HMPE core.
f: Inspect mooring line jackets before and during use and retire or repair damaged lines.

t: Interviewee gave the wrong oil spill drill duty (first aid kit and stretcher) when the muster list assigned lifeboat preparation and gas detector.
f: Check your muster list duty for each emergency and know it before an inspector asks.

t: Company procedure did not define spare parts or calibration gas quantities for gas detectors, only saying 'sufficient'.
f: Keep an inventory of calibration gases and spares with minimum stock levels and expiry dates.

t: The PMS had no separate periodic task for checking fire prevention on machinery space hot surfaces, and no ship-specific checklist existed.
f: Set up a PMS task with a ship-specific checklist for hot surface and leak inspections.

t: The uploaded photo showed the port side instead of the starboard side requested; the condition itself was not a concern.
f: Double-check side and location labels before uploading inspection photos.

t: The uploaded photo showed the starboard side instead of the port side requested; the condition itself was not a concern.
f: Label photos by side and area when taking them to avoid upload mix-ups.

t: A shore calibration of the oily water separator equipment had not been recorded in the Oil Record Book.
f: Record OWS and oil content meter calibrations and servicing in the ORB.

t: The ballast pump room housed a nitrogen buffer tank, but its low oxygen alarm sounded only in the CCR, not locally in the space.
f: Test low-oxygen alarms both locally and remotely for any space containing nitrogen equipment.

t: There was no local oxygen readout at the entrance to the ballast pump room, although the space held a nitrogen buffer tank.
f: Check oxygen levels before entering any space with nitrogen equipment, using a portable meter if needed.

t: The company entry permit set the benzene TLV at 1 ppm, whereas ACGIH, ILO and WHO references give 0.5 ppm.
f: Check permit exposure limits against current references and query outdated values with the office.

t: Water-resistant engine starting and operating instructions were not posted near the boat engine controls; fitted before the inspector left.
f: Make sure lifeboat and rescue boat engines have durable starting instructions posted at the controls.

t: Bridge officer was unfamiliar with the NAVAREA warning procedure; NAVAREA I warnings in force were missing and GMDSS was not set to receive them.
f: Set EGC receivers for the current NAVAREA and keep a file of warnings in force.

t: Also logged as a learning gap: NAVAREA I warnings in force were not on board and the GMDSS receivers were not configured for that area.
f: Check receiver area settings when entering a new NAVAREA and log the warnings in force.

t: Alarm settings on the cargo tank secondary venting pressure sensors did not match company requirements for the discharge mode in use.
f: Adjust tank pressure alarm set points for each operation (loading, discharging with IG) per the company table.

t: The CCR officer had not set the required tank pressure alarm settings for discharging with inert gas; corrected before the inspector left.
f: Make alarm set point changes part of the pre-discharge checklist.

t: Load line certificate showed winter and WNA marks not on the hull (WNA not applicable over 100 m), and IOPP Form B left fitted items unticked.
f: Cross-check certificate and IOPP supplement entries against the ship's actual marks and fittings.

t: The cargo and ballast valve test record had no provision to check that local and remote valve position indicators agreed.
f: When testing hydraulic valves, compare local and remote position indicators and record the result.

t: One anchor had been lost; this was reported to class and recorded in the defect system pending replacement.
f: Keep class and the office informed of lost equipment and track the replacement plan.

t: Class had issued a conditional safety construction certificate because of the lost anchor.
f: Track conditional certificates' validity and the actions needed to clear them before expiry.

t: One of the main deck emergency lights was not working.
f: Test emergency lighting regularly and replace failed lamps straight away.

t: Earth cables to the bridge wing searchlights were broken; repaired once pointed out.
f: Check earthing and cabling of deck electrical equipment during routine inspections.

t: Brake drums on the starboard poop deck mooring winches were heavily rusted and uneven.
f: Keep winch brake drums clean and free of corrosion, as poor drum condition affects brake holding.

t: 21 NAVTEX stations were selected, most irrelevant to the ship's position off Ulsan, Korea; reset to stations within 250-400 nm.
f: Select only NAVTEX stations covering your area and update the selection as the voyage goes on.

t: The inert gas scrubber was not identified as an enclosed space; corrected by the engine team during the inspection.
f: Keep the enclosed spaces list complete and mark all such spaces, including the IG scrubber.

t: Interviewee could not explain the difference between X-band and S-band radar or in which conditions S-band works better.
f: Know that S-band copes better with rain and sea clutter, while X-band gives finer detail on small targets.

t: Interviewee could not state the height at which work-at-height controls apply and was unfamiliar with the precautions in the work aloft risk assessment.
f: Know the company's working-aloft height threshold and the key controls in the RA before starting the job.

t: Mercaptan detector tubes on board were below the company minimum of 10; interviewee did not know the minimum stock and missed it in the inventory.
f: Keep a detector tube inventory with minimum stock levels and expiry dates and reorder early.

t: Seizings on six fire and foam hoses had deteriorated and the binding wires were corroded.
f: Inspect hose couplings and seizings during fire equipment checks and renew corroded bindings.

t: Interviewee admitted missing the condition of the fire and foam hoses during the last recorded safety inspection.
f: Unroll and check hoses and couplings properly during safety inspections, not just count them.

t: Entry procedures set no extra precautions for ballast tanks treated by an electrolysis BWTS; crew relied on a maker statement that no chlorine check was needed.
f: Ask the office to assess BWTS by-products such as chlorine and add any extra checks to the entry permit.

t: During pump room rounds, two safety chains guarding open vertical ladder accesses were unhooked and had been overlooked.
f: Check that guard chains at ladder openings are in place every time you pass through the pump room.

t: Bunkering procedures did not require checking bunker tank ullage spaces for flammable vapour before, during or after bunkering.
f: Include flammable vapour checks of bunker tank ullage spaces in the bunker plan and checklist.

t: The starboard lifeboat's suspension blocks were not seated on the davit horns, leaving a gap of about 5 cm; corrected during the inspection.
f: After recovering the lifeboat, check the suspension blocks are fully seated on the davit horns.

t: The officer had overlooked during routine inspection that the lifeboat suspension blocks were not seated on the davit horns.
f: Include the boat's stowed position (blocks, gripes, lashings) in weekly LSA checks.

t: The crude oil MSDS received at the load port had only 9 sections instead of the 16 required by IMO MSC.286(86), and this went unnoticed.
f: Check each cargo safety data sheet has all 16 sections and ask the terminal for a complete one if not.

t: No records were on board of the previous marine superintendent inspection, so the interval between visits and shore review could not be checked.
f: Keep copies of previous superintendent inspection reports on board for review.

t: Several HVPQ entries were wrong: CAP survey areas did not match the CAP certificate, and mooring layout, bow mooring and manifold diagrams were missing.
f: Cross-check HVPQ entries against certificates and attach all required diagrams before the inspection.

t: The port ECDIS could not load the Chart 1 (S-57) symbol display despite repeated tries; shore support was needed and it was fixed by the closing meeting.
f: Practise opening the Chart 1 symbol library on each ECDIS so you can show it on demand.

t: A cargo stripping line flange was leaking cargo at 1-2 drops per second during discharge; repaired by the closing meeting.
f: Check cargo line flanges regularly during operations and stop and repair any leak at once.

t: The breathing air compressor filling SCBA, EEBD and lifeboat air cylinders had one relief valve at 320 bar, above the 300, 200 and 150 bar cylinder ratings.
f: Know the compressor's relief settings and how to fill lower-pressure cylinders without over-pressurising.

t: When boarding at anchor by boat, the inspector found the outboard corner stanchion missing from the gangway's bottom platform; fitted once pointed out.
f: Check the bottom platform stanchions and rails of the accommodation ladder before every boat transfer.

t: An aft mooring winch was leaking hydraulic oil from its control lever at 3-4 drops per second; a spare block was on board and repair was planned.
f: Repair hydraulic leaks on deck machinery promptly and contain any oil on deck.

t: Interviewee could not explain why fire doors are fitted, how the types differ or where to find more information.
f: Know the fire door types on board and where they are shown on the fire control plan.

t: Second record of the same gap: interviewee did not know the fire door types or where to find them on the fire and safety plan.
f: Study the fire and safety plan legend so you can point out fire door types and locations.

t: A bridge deck fire hydrant valve could not be opened by hand; the crew member only managed it on a second try using a wheel spanner.
f: Exercise and grease fire hydrant valves regularly so they can be opened by hand.

t: The inspection records section of the Permanent Means of Access Manual (SOLAS II-1/3-6) was blank; tank inspection reports also left out access items.
f: Record the condition of ladders, platforms and steps in the PMA Manual after each tank inspection.

t: Enclosed space entry procedures had not been revised for the enhanced CO2 monitoring in IMO MSC.581(110).
f: Check your entry permit includes CO2 testing per MSC.581(110) and raise it with the office if not.

t: A short-term BWM certificate was in force because the BWTS had failed; it required a risk assessment, contingency measures, coastal state notice and BWRB entries.
f: Know the conditions on any short-term certificate and keep evidence that each one is being met.

t: The International Ballast Water Management Certificate on board was a short-term certificate valid for only two months.
f: Track short-term certificate expiry and the repairs needed to obtain a full-term certificate.

t: Non-slip coating on the deck and mooring areas fore and aft was in very poor condition.
f: Renew non-slip paint in mooring stations and walkways as part of planned maintenance.

t: Deck service pipes for water, ballast and tank cleaning were rusted and badly corroded at clamps and supports; two ballast gauge glasses in the pump room were broken.
f: Prioritise corrosion at pipe clamps and supports and replace broken gauge glasses.

t: Engine room and stores were dirty, with spares left on the floor, behind machinery and beside safety equipment; a main engine thermometer glass was broken.
f: Keep spares secured in stores, clear of safety equipment, and replace broken instruments.

t: The engine room was generally untidy and dirty, looking older than the ship's actual age.
f: Keep a regular engine room cleaning routine; housekeeping is the first thing inspectors notice.

t: The C/E, 2/E and 3/E in the control room could not locate the company procedures the inspector asked about.
f: Practise finding key SMS procedures quickly, especially those for your own department.

t: Engineers' familiarisation with where procedures sit in the SMS was judged insufficient, as they struggled to find them.
f: Include finding your way around the SMS in joining familiarisation.

t: Only two personal gas detectors were carried for a crew of 22, not enough for normal work and with no spare for an emergency entry.
f: Match personal gas detector numbers to the people working in hazardous areas at once, plus spares.

t: A fireman's outfit mixed an aluminised hood with a cotton suit, the helmet was not marked as approved, and the station was cluttered with old spares.
f: Keep each fireman's outfit complete, matching and approved, with the fire station kept clear.

t: Lifeboat painter was hard to release, its handle unmarked and nobody assigned to it; the port pilot ladder's securing rope was crumbling with a poor splice.
f: Mark painter release gear, assign it on the muster list and check pilot ladder securing ropes.

t: No crew member was assigned to release the painter from either lifeboat, and the task was not shown in the emergency plan.
f: Assign painter release as a named muster list duty for each lifeboat.

t: Safety goggles in the battery locker and safety equipment locker had perished elastic straps, making them unusable.
f: Check PPE in lockers regularly and replace goggles with perished straps.

t: Four cargo hoses stowed in the forward store were not tagged with their status or details.
f: Tag every cargo hose with its ID, test date and status (in service or condemned).

t: Lock-out/tag-out records used generic terms such as 'hydraulic lock out' instead of naming the actual equipment isolated.
f: Name the specific equipment and isolation points on every LOTO record.

t: Procedures did not require a working overside/aloft checklist for routine rescue boat launches, and launch records showed none was used.
f: Use the working overside checklist for every rescue boat launch, including routine drills.

t: The shaft power limitation panel showed a lost-connection alarm because the torque meter had gone ashore for calibration; no defect report existed.
f: Raise a defect report whenever equipment is landed for repair or calibration.

t: At least four calibration (span) gas bottles for the portable gas detectors had expired.
f: Check calibration gas expiry dates monthly and reorder before they lapse.

t: The expired span gases had not been removed, and an inventory sheet revised later still listed them as available.
f: Remove expired calibration gases from use and keep the inventory sheet accurate.

t: In the ballast pump room, the cable protection at the BWTS UV reactor joint was loose and taped, with cables visible inside.
f: Repair damaged cable glands and conduits properly; tape is not an acceptable fix.

t: The safety inspection of the ballast pump room was ineffective: there was no record of the damaged BWTS cable protection.
f: Write down every defect found on safety rounds so it is tracked to repair.

t: The BWTS was out of order because of a UV power unit fault alarm.
f: Report BWTS failures promptly and follow the ballast water contingency measures in the BWMP.

t: The terminal's pre-operation checklist could not be produced when the inspector asked for it.
f: Keep charterer and terminal checklists completed and filed so they can be shown on request.

t: When engine departure checklists were reviewed, the one for the latest departure could not be found.
f: File completed departure and arrival checklists straight away so the latest is always available.

t: The latest edition of the COLREG publication was not on board; an older 2023 edition was held.
f: Check bridge publications against the latest editions list and order replacements in good time.

t: Interviewee had not checked bridge publications for new editions, saying supply was the shore office's responsibility.
f: Own the publications check on board: the office supplies, but the ship must spot what is out of date.

t: A heaving line was kept attached to the lifebuoy at the pilot boarding station, contrary to the ICS Bridge Procedures Guide checklist; interviewee was unaware.
f: Set up the pilot boarding station exactly as the BPG pilot boarding checklist describes.

t: Open/close markings on the CO2 room vent head handwheel were painted over; interviewee said its location meant it was missed on rounds.
f: Keep open/shut markings on vents and closing devices visible and never paint over them.

t: Operator procedure applied CATZOC and tide corrections only to UKC calculations, not to the safety depth setting.
f: Allow for CATZOC accuracy and tide when setting ECDIS safety depth, not just for UKC.

t: Cargo line pressure testing was queried: the annual test was at the 16 bar working pressure, while the last 24 bar design-pressure test was done by the yard.
f: Know your cargo line test regime (annual and 1.5x tests) and record the pressure used each time.

t: Class recorded hull damage from a barge contact (shell set-in up to 30 mm, bent frames in a ballast tank), to be re-examined at dry dock; HVPQ/PIQ were updated.
f: After any contact damage, notify class, track the class condition and update the HVPQ and PIQ.

t: One of the acetylene cylinders stored on the poop deck was covered in hard rust.
f: Inspect gas cylinders in storage for corrosion and send badly rusted ones ashore.

t: The last safety inspection rounds were ineffective, as the heavily rusted acetylene cylinder had not been noticed.
f: Include gas cylinder condition and stowage in deck safety rounds.

t: Same finding logged as custom and practice: the rusted acetylene cylinder had been passed over on routine safety rounds.
f: Look at stored cylinders closely each round instead of assuming nothing has changed.

t: The uploaded photo showed the cargo tank's ordinary P/V devices instead of the requested item; the correct photo was taken at the inspection.
f: Check each uploaded photo matches the exact equipment named in the requirement.

t: A main deck mooring winch used for the aft breast lines had no brake setting mark on the brake.
f: Make sure every winch brake has a clear mark showing its set position from the brake test.

t: The cargo watch officer could not explain the ship/shore safety checklist repetitive check on electrical insulation, although it had been ticked.
f: Never tick a checklist item you cannot explain; know how each SSSCL repetitive check is verified.

t: The bunker analysis report tested against ISO 8217:2005 although the fuel had been ordered to ISO 8217:2017.
f: Check the bunker analysis quotes the same ISO 8217 edition as the stem and query any mismatch.

t: A junior engineer did not know what the resuscitator kit contained, and a junior officer did not know the oxygen content of its cylinder.
f: Open the resuscitator kit during drills and learn its contents and cylinder capacity.

t: The ship's record showed a past USCG detention: an expanded ISM exam found defects were not being identified and fixed (leaking tank hatches, taped hoses, unlagged hot pipes).
f: Find, report and fix defects through the SMS before PSC does; inspectors review past detentions.

t: The company entry permit did not follow MSC.581(110) on who completes each section; the C/O signed the preparation and checks and was also an entrant.
f: Know who must authorise, check and enter under the revised permit, and keep those roles separate.

t: The interviewee's preparation of the enclosed space entry permit did not follow the revised IMO recommendations (MSC.581(110)).
f: Fill in entry permits as the revised IMO recommendations require, with the right person signing each part.

t: Emergency plans covered flooding only generically; there were no plans for machinery space, pump room or forecastle flooding or a hull breach.
f: Check contingency plans exist for each flooding scenario relevant to your ship, and drill them.

t: A fixed oxygen sensor in the engine room inert gas space was defective; it was found on arrival and still being troubleshot.
f: Test fixed oxygen sensors before arrival and report failures with interim measures in place.

t: Fixed gauging for one cargo tank read 1.38 m ullage while the UTI showed 5.27 m; it failed on arrival and was fixed before the inspection ended.
f: Compare fixed gauges with UTI readings regularly, especially before starting cargo operations.

t: Annual, intermediate and class attendance survey reports had not been filed for several years; they were printed and filed during the inspection.
f: File class survey reports in the survey file as soon as they are received.

t: HVPQ entries were out of date for the last PSC inspection, last ballast tank inspection and last winch brake test.
f: Update the HVPQ after every PSC, tank inspection and brake test, not just before vetting.

t: Free-fall lifeboat manoeuvring drills were recorded without the boat being released from its falls, contrary to the guidelines.
f: Follow the guidelines for free-fall boat release and manoeuvring and record what was actually done.

t: Interviewee did not know the company procedure for six-monthly free-fall or simulated launching of the lifeboat with its assigned crew.
f: Know your free-fall lifeboat launch schedule and the simulated launch method.

t: One of the portable multi-gas meters had been landed ashore for maintenance; a defect report was raised.
f: Keep enough working gas meters on board while one is ashore, and ask for a loan unit if needed.

t: The second portable gas meter read 3.5 ppm H2S on 25 ppm test gas and showed no CO reading; sensors were renewed during the inspection.
f: Bump test gas meters before each use and replace failing sensors straight away.

t: Flame screens on vent pipes from the block and bleed valve system were damaged.
f: Include flame screens on all vents in the PMS and inspect them regularly.

t: The fresh water generator ejector line had a temporary weld build-up repair and no defect had been raised.
f: Record every temporary repair as a defect until a permanent repair is done.

t: The engineer responsible had not raised a defect for the temporary repair on the seawater line.
f: Log temporary repairs in the defect system so the office can plan a permanent fix.

t: The uploaded photo showed the port manifold looking forward to aft, not the view requested.
f: Take repository photos from the exact angle and side specified.

t: Another uploaded photo also showed the port side manifold instead of the required view.
f: Check photo uploads against the requirement before submitting.

t: The HVPQ stated 7 deck ratings for mooring operations while the crew list showed 6.
f: Update manning figures in the HVPQ whenever crew numbers change.

t: A deck light on the aft port side had water collected inside its cover.
f: Check deck light covers and seals during rounds and drain and reseal leaking fittings.

t: The interviewee had not checked the condition of deck lighting during the safety inspection.
f: Include deck light fittings in safety rounds.

t: Cargo heating steam pipes near a cargo tank were rusted, especially at flanges and valves, and one valve handwheel was missing.
f: Keep heating line valves complete with handwheels and treat corrosion at flanges early.

t: The interviewee had missed the condition of the heating pipework during the deck safety inspection.
f: Look at pipework, flanges and valves item by item during deck inspections.

t: No written process covered document control: the certificate index form was not sent ashore, and uploads to the company's SMS software were not described.
f: Know how certificates are tracked on board and ashore, and who checks expiry dates.

t: A public toilet on the accommodation deck was out of order awaiting spare parts.
f: Report accommodation defects too, and track spares until the repair is done.

t: The toilet failure had not been entered in the defect reporting system.
f: Every defect, however minor, goes in the defect reporting system.

t: Neither the procedures nor the PMS reflected the maker's two-yearly ECDIS hard drive replacement, and no replacement was recorded.
f: Put maker-required ECDIS maintenance, such as hard drive renewal, into the PMS.

t: Interviewee was not aware of the maker's requirement to replace the ECDIS hard drive every two years.
f: Read the ECDIS maker's maintenance section and know its periodic tasks.

t: A free-fall lifeboat launch and manoeuvre was recorded, but a crew member listed as on board said nobody boarded and the boat was not released.
f: Record drills exactly as carried out; false drill records are a serious finding.

t: Interviewee had not noticed the recovery motor left fitted on the aft emergency towing wire winch, contrary to the maker's instructions.
f: Stow emergency towing gear as the maker and towing booklet describe, and check it on rounds.

t: HVPQ had outdated dates, a manning figure that did not match the Minimum Safe Manning Certificate, and the BWTS listed as chemical instead of filtration/electrolysis.
f: Review the HVPQ line by line against certificates and equipment before each update.

t: A ballast pump in the pump room had a slight water leak from its casing flange, with water pooling on the deck plating.
f: Report pump leaks promptly and keep pump room plating and bilges dry.

t: No local instruction at the emergency generator explained the changeover between its primary and secondary battery banks.
f: Post clear operating instructions at emergency equipment, including battery changeover.

t: The navigation assessment report did not include the assessor's qualifications and seagoing experience; these were only produced at the end of the inspection.
f: Make sure assessor qualifications are written into each navigation assessment report.

t: The port lifeboat's compressed air cylinder leaked when pressurised; repaired by the end of the inspection.
f: Pressurise and leak-check lifeboat air support systems as part of routine LSA testing.

t: The lifeboat air cylinder was recorded as tested weekly, yet it leaked, so the weekly checks could not be shown to be effective.
f: Carry out each step of the weekly LSA check properly; ticking the record is not testing.

t: Recent entry permits had no CO2 check though CO2 detector tubes were on board unused, and the interviewee did not know the safe CO2 reading for entry.
f: Use the CO2 tubes or meter for entry checks and know the CO2 limit for safe entry.

t: Portable gas detectors gave erratic cargo tank readings of 1.6% O2, far below the actual level; after recalibration in the CCR they misread again on deck.
f: If a gas meter reads erratically, take it out of use, use a backup and report the fault.

t: The liquid level in the inert gas line P/V breaker could not be seen because the sight glass was dirty.
f: Keep sight glasses on the P/V breaker and deck seal clean so liquid levels can be checked.

t: The P/V breaker level was unreadable, yet the officer had recorded in the SSSCL and pre-arrival checks that the IG system was in good order.
f: Only sign checklist items you have physically verified, including levels in sight glasses.

t: Also logged as custom and practice: IG system checks were signed off routinely although the breaker level could not be read.
f: Treat repetitive checklist items as real checks each time, not a habit of ticking.

t: There was no formal procedure for the office to acknowledge defects reported by the ship; acknowledgement was sometimes by email and sometimes absent.
f: Follow up unacknowledged defect reports with the office and keep the replies on file.

t: The PIQ declared no lost time injury in the last 12 months, but records showed one, a crew member struck by a wave on deck.
f: Check incident and injury records before answering PIQ safety questions.

t: An engine room escape hatch to the upper deck was locked from inside with no way to open it from the deck side; unlocked during the inspection.
f: Keep escape hatches operable from both sides; never lock them shut.

t: The crew had secured the escape hatch from inside, leaving no access for a fire party from the weather deck.
f: Check escape hatches can be opened from both sides during safety rounds.

t: The uploaded photo of the aft emergency towing gear was taken with the canvas cover on, so it did not show the actual condition.
f: Remove covers before taking condition photos so the equipment itself is visible.

t: The latest cargo pump hydraulic oil analysis was satisfactory, but the previous one had shown high particle counts.
f: Act on adverse oil analysis results with filtering or renewal, and record what was done.

t: Interviewee knew of the new IMO CO2 testing requirement, but the procedure was not updated and the last entry permit had no CO2 check.
f: Test and record CO2 for entries where the risk exists, even before the permit form is updated.

t: There was no procedure for inspecting, electrically testing or replacing electrical insulating gloves.
f: Inspect insulating gloves before each use and track their test or replacement dates.

t: With only one MGO storage tank, new and old bunker batches were mixed and burnt before analysis results came, with no risk assessment, approval or compatibility test.
f: Avoid commingling bunkers; if unavoidable, test compatibility and get a risk assessment approved first.

t: Also logged as custom and practice: commingling and using untested bunkers was treated as routine because only one MGO tank was available.
f: Plan bunker tank segregation before bunkering so new fuel can be held until analysis results arrive.

t: Checklists showed remote steering controls tested from each position before arrival and departure, but they were not; the officer did not know the bridge wing NFU controls existed.
f: Test steering from every control position, including bridge wing NFU, before arrival and departure.

t: Company policy allowed all principal fire drill scenarios to be covered over twelve months instead of six.
f: Plan fire drills so every principal scenario is covered within the expected six-month cycle.

t: No cargo pump room fire drill had been held in the last twelve months, as company policy required.
f: Track drill scenarios on a planner so none, such as a pump room fire, gets missed.

t: The responsible officer had not confirmed that loose lifting gear (chain blocks, slings, shackles) was tested at the 30-month interval set by company policy.
f: Keep a register of loose lifting gear with test dates and remove overdue items from use.

t: No procedure covered the Ozone-depleting Substances Record Book and none was on board, although the IAPP showed no such substances were fitted.
f: Check the IAPP supplement to see whether an ODS Record Book is needed, and know why if not.

t: The inspector got a full safety briefing at the gangway, but the CBP officer boarding right after was not briefed.
f: Give every visitor the gangway safety briefing, including officials who seem in a hurry.

t: A mooring rope used as a headline on the forecastle was weather-damaged with broken strands.
f: Inspect lines before use and do not send out ropes with broken strands.

t: The responsible officer had used the damaged rope as a headline at this port.
f: Check line condition when preparing for mooring and swap out damaged lines.

t: No water-resistant starting and operating instructions were posted near the rescue boat engine controls; printed and posted during the inspection.
f: Check durable engine operating instructions are posted in each survival craft.

t: The monthly safety inspection had not picked up the missing rescue boat engine instructions.
f: Include required notices and instructions in the monthly LSA inspection checklist.

t: There was no calibration gas for measuring hydrocarbon by volume in inerted atmospheres; a requisition had been raised.
f: Keep calibration gas for every gas meter range in use, including HC % by volume.

t: Several bolts on BWTS explosion-proof enclosures were missing or broken, up to seven on a single box.
f: Check every bolt on flameproof enclosures is fitted and tight, and replace missing ones at once.

t: The port pilot ladder had broken strands at three points; a replacement had been requisitioned.
f: Take pilot ladders with damaged side ropes out of service until replaced.

t: The officer inspecting the BWTS had missed the broken bolts and recorded all explosion-proof fittings as in good order.
f: Count and check flameproof enclosure bolts during inspections rather than taking a quick look.

t: The audible alarm at the port entrance to the nitrogen generator room was not working; a defect had been raised.
f: Test O2 alarms at nitrogen room entrances regularly and post warnings while they are defective.

t: Brake mechanisms, pins and brackets on six mooring winches fore and aft were heavily rusted; maintenance was in progress.
f: Keep winch brake linkages greased and free of corrosion so the brakes work properly.

t: A required photo had not been uploaded to the repository.
f: Check the photo upload list is complete before the inspection.

t: The HVPQ did not show that fixed gas detection covered the ballast tanks, and cargo pump temperature sensor entries were wrongly tabulated.
f: Have the C/O and C/E check HVPQ technical entries against the actual equipment.

t: The mooring familiarisation checklist was only for crew new to mooring, so none had used it, despite the ship's uncommon hydraulic winch brakes.
f: Do ship-specific familiarisation on unusual equipment, like hydraulic winch brakes, whatever your experience.

t: The uploaded picture of the emergency towing wire stowage had the canvas cover on.
f: Remove covers before taking photos so the inspector can see the gear's real condition.

t: The PMS required six-monthly steering gear hydraulic oil analysis, but the latest report on board was about a year old.
f: Track oil sampling dates in the PMS and land samples on time.

t: The entry procedure and permit did not include CO2 testing as per IMO MSC.581(110), although the ship mainly carried organic cargoes.
f: Include CO2 in entry gas testing, especially on ships carrying organic cargoes.

t: No instrument able to measure CO2 before enclosed space entry was on board, and there was no sign one had been ordered.
f: Check your gas meters cover CO2 and raise a requisition early if they do not.

t: No personal gas detectors able to measure CO2 during entry were on board, with no evidence of any being ordered.
f: Make sure entrants carry personal monitors covering CO2 as well as O2, HC, H2S and CO.

t: The engine room water mist automatic start test was done quarterly instead of monthly as MSC.1/Circ.1432 requires.
f: Set PMS intervals for fire system tests to match MSC.1/Circ.1432 and maker requirements.

t: The Enhanced Survey File lacked class attendance reports for two years and did not document survey status after the last dry dock.
f: Keep the Enhanced Survey File complete with every class report and the post-dry dock survey status.

t: The pressure gauge on a heavy fuel oil purifier heater in the engine room was not working.
f: Replace defective gauges promptly and include gauges in engine room rounds.

t: Old vent heads and a spare box had been lashed on an outside deck since dry dock, and their lashings were not covered by the safety inspection checklist.
f: Land or properly stow redundant items, and include any deck lashings in safety inspections.

t: The oxygen repeater at one nitrogen generator room entrance read 21.1% while the actual level was 20.9%, showing it was inaccurate.
f: Compare O2 repeaters with the main sensor and calibrate any that disagree.

t: The PMS had no task to verify or calibrate the oxygen repeaters at the nitrogen generator room entrances.
f: Add O2 repeater checks and calibration to the PMS.

t: Heat-resistant coating on the steam return observation tank was peeling while heated cargo was being discharged.
f: Maintain heat-resistant coatings on steam system tanks and lines as part of planned maintenance.

t: Navigation procedures gave no guidance on when to use the full ECDIS display layer or on extending the look-ahead in low-accuracy CATZOC (B, C, D, U) areas.
f: Know when to switch to the full ECDIS display and widen safety margins in poor CATZOC areas.

t: The AIS procedure treated low power in port as enough to avoid static risk and ignored automatic polling, contrary to ISGOTT 6 section 4.13.4.
f: Follow ISGOTT for AIS at terminals: switch off, isolate the aerial or use a dummy load.

t: Drill procedures and records did not capture safety precautions for the drill, lessons for the contingency plan, or attached risk assessments and permits.
f: Record drill safety precautions and lessons learnt, and attach any RA or permits used.

t: Entry procedures did not meet MSC.581(110) on CO2 testing and monitors, shore personnel interface with a joint RA, or a written rescue plan.
f: Know the main MSC.581(110) changes: CO2 testing, shore staff entries and a written rescue plan.

t: Personal gas monitors able to measure CO2, with their span gases, had not been supplied; a requisition had been raised.
f: Follow up requisitions for CO2 monitors and keep interim entry controls in place meanwhile.

t: A sacrificial flange on an LT cooler was leaking at about 10 drops a minute; fixed before the inspection ended.
f: Check cooler flanges on engine room rounds and fix weeps before they grow.

t: Cruciform bollards near the four vapour manifolds were not in line with the manifolds, pad eyes and chocks used for securing hoses.
f: Know how hose hang-off chains are secured at each manifold and report layout limits to the office.

t: Company limits were 2 MOhm (220 V) and 5 MOhm (440 V), but the earth fault meters only read below 1 MOhm; this was known but no new meters were ordered.
f: If fitted instruments cannot show company limits, report it and raise a requisition.

t: No cruciform bollard was fitted in line, or nearly in line, with the vapour manifolds to secure the hose hang-off chain.
f: Report manifold layout shortfalls to the office so permanent fittings can be added.

t: After the enhanced special survey, the survey statement, Executive Hull Summary and Hull Survey Programme were not on board.
f: Ask class for the survey documents straight after a special survey and file them in the survey file.

t: Interviewee was unfamiliar with the company procedure for maintaining the Enhanced Survey File and its records.
f: Know what the Enhanced Survey File must contain and who is responsible for it.

t: Entry procedures missed key MSC.581(110) items: personal CO2 monitors, warning signs and a safe/unsafe spaces diagram at access points, and CO2 danger levels.
f: Post enclosed space signs and a spaces diagram, and know the CO2 danger levels for entry.

t: No entry permit since MSC.581(110) took effect recorded CO2, signs and the spaces diagram were not posted, and the interviewee was unaware of the requirement.
f: Keep up with new IMO entry rules even before company procedures change, and raise gaps.

t: None of the five personal and two portable gas detectors on board had a CO2 sensor, so CO2 could not be tested for entry.
f: Check your gas instruments cover every gas required for entry, including CO2.

t: Interviewee was not aware of the MSC.581(110) requirements for CO2 testing before entry or for carrying CO2-capable instruments.
f: Learn the key changes in MSC.581(110) on enclosed space entry.

t: Flywheel guards on two auxiliary engines had gaps of about 40 cm and 20 cm, exposing rotating parts; this had not been noticed on routine rounds.
f: Check machinery guards for gaps during rounds and add guarding where hands could reach moving parts.

t: There was no procedure for checking the accuracy of the electromagnetic speed log or what reference to compare it against.
f: Check the EM log against speed over ground while allowing for current and wind, and record results.

t: Interviewee's 3-monthly speed log check compared speed through water with true speed without allowing for current or wind, which is not a valid test.
f: Use a proper log check method, such as reciprocal runs, so current effects cancel out.

t: Interviewee did not know when high-level or overfill alarms may be isolated under company procedure or what safeguards are then needed.
f: Know the conditions for isolating tank level alarms and the extra controls needed while isolated.

t: Photo not representative: steam traps on a cargo tank's heating coils were heavily rusted, although this was already on the dry dock defect list.
f: Make sure uploaded photos show current condition, including known defects awaiting dry dock.

t: The online HVPQ had not been updated for a change of flag, port of registry, owner and P&I club made months earlier.
f: Update the HVPQ straight after any change of flag, ownership or P&I.

t: Two findings from the Master's quarterly navigation assessment were closed with evidence but still showed open and overdue in the company's SMS software.
f: Close findings in the company system as well as by email, and check the status updates.

t: On the bridge navigation light panel, the aft anchor light's secondary lamp was not working and showed an alarm.
f: Test main and standby navigation lights from the panel and fix failed lamps before sailing.

t: The cargo tank gauging display in the CCR showed 'ERROR' for the sensors on three cargo tanks.
f: Report gauging faults at once and agree alternative ullaging methods before cargo work.

t: Steam heating lines on deck were rusted and unpainted, a condensate tank sight glass was broken, and one hydraulic power pack motor had been out for months.
f: Keep heating lines painted, replace broken sight glasses and chase long-pending spares.

t: The steering gear room had wooden shelves with spares in wooden boxes and loose old equipment, not secured.
f: Keep the steering gear room clear of combustible storage and secure all spares for sea.

t: Alcohol test equipment training ran every six months, so a senior officer on a four-month contract might never be trained while on board.
f: Train new joiners on alcohol testing equipment during familiarisation, not only at fixed intervals.

t: An engine room fire hydrant was placed about 60 cm from a purifier motor, facing it, so opening it could spray seawater onto the motor.
f: Report hydrants placed where they could spray electrical equipment, and fit a shield if needed.

t: Self-igniting lights on two boat deck lifebuoys were not intrinsically safe, against the operator's policy for equipment outside the accommodation.
f: Check lifebuoy lights used in hazardous areas are intrinsically safe types.

t: Class had added a statutory condition requiring a CO2 gas detector for enclosed space entry, with interim safety measures until it was supplied.
f: Know any open class conditions, their due dates and the interim measures in place.

t: The generator engines' SCR system was out of service after urea dosing pump and urea leak alarms, and was stopped while the ship was inside an ECA.
f: Know the reporting steps when NOx abatement equipment fails inside an ECA.

t: The SCR failure was not reported to class, flag or the arrival port; the company only informed the flag at the closing meeting and a dispensation followed.
f: Report SCR or other emission equipment failures to flag, class and port authorities without delay.

t: Interviewee did not know the SCR had to be running inside the ECA, and its failure was not reported to the Master or the company.
f: Report any emission control failure to the Master and office immediately, especially in an ECA.

t: Interviewee could not explain the company's response to a cargo leak into a double hull space or where the hose for inerting that space was kept.
f: Know the cargo-leak-into-double-hull contingency plan and where the inerting hose is kept.

t: Also logged under procedures: the double hull cargo leak procedure and location of the inerting connection were not understood.
f: Walk through the double hull leak plan, including rigging the inerting hose, during drills.

t: Portable and personal gas meters covered O2, CO, H2S and HC, but none could measure CO2 as MSC.581(110) expects.
f: Make sure CO2 detection is available before any enclosed space entry.

t: Neither the entry checklist nor the procedures required testing for CO2 as per MSC.581(110).
f: Check the entry checklist includes CO2 and ask the office for an updated form if not.

t: Hydraulic oil was dripping continuously from connections at the port mooring winch and windlass speed control levers.
f: Fix hydraulic leaks at deck machinery controls promptly and keep drip trays clean.

t: Interviewee had overlooked the winch and windlass hydraulic leak during the safety inspection; it was fixed once pointed out.
f: Check deck machinery controls and fittings for leaks during each safety inspection.

t: Interviewee was not aware of the requirement to carry a Coating Technical File approved by the Administration.
f: Know which statutory files must be on board, including the Coating Technical File.

t: Two senior officers new to the operator joined with no overlap, as their reliefs left the same day, against the operator's handover and parallel sailing rules.
f: Flag crew change plans that break overlap or handover rules to the office before they happen.

t: Interviewee did not know the company rules on engine room manning for narrow channels, heavy weather and port approaches; nothing was logged for these periods.
f: Know when the engine room must be manned and by whom, and record it in the engine log.

t: A fault on the wheelhouse fire detection panel delayed alarms at the main panel and ECR repeater; a system upgrade was pending in the defect system.
f: Test that fire alarms sound promptly at every panel and repeater, and chase pending fixes.

t: Only one portable multi-gas meter was on board instead of the two required; an order had been placed.
f: Keep the required number of working gas meters and report shortfalls straight away.

t: Two UTI tapes had last been calibrated more than three years earlier; interviewee kept no record and did not know annual calibration was required.
f: Keep a calibration log for UTI tapes and send them for calibration every year.

t: Interviewee did not know ear protection was needed when starting the emergency generator, and its door had no ear protection sign.
f: Wear ear protection in noisy machinery spaces and post IMO safety signs at their entrances.

t: The external audible and visual alert for the telephone at the main engine local control station was not working; fixed before the inspection ended.
f: Test communication links and their alerts at the engine local control station regularly.

t: Interviewee had not noticed that the telephone alerts at the main engine local control station were not working.
f: Include emergency communication tests in engine room routines.

t: The operator's entry policy had not been updated to require CO2 testing as part of the permit process under MSC.581(110).
f: Check your permit includes CO2 and raise the gap with the office if the policy lags behind.

t: The ship had no instrument capable of measuring CO2.
f: Make sure a CO2-capable gas meter or tubes are on board for enclosed space entry checks.

t: The pilot access stanchions at deck level had no means of being secured at their upper part, as required.
f: Check pilot boarding stanchions are rigidly secured at both the base and the upper part.

t: Interviewee did not know that pilot ladder stanchions must be secured at both the lower and upper parts.
f: Know the rigging requirements for pilot access points, including how stanchions are fixed.

t: The officer had not signed the terminal declaration of inspection at the change of watch as required.
f: Sign the declaration of inspection at each watch change when the terminal requires it.

t: On one STS day the Master and C/O had less than 10 hours' rest in 24 hours; records showed compensatory rest was taken.
f: Plan STS work around rest hours and record any exception and compensatory rest properly.

t: Only the AED's monthly self-tests were recorded; the periodic maintenance in the maker's manual was not being followed.
f: Follow the AED maker's full maintenance schedule, not just the automatic self-test.

t: The ballast capacity on the BWM certificate differed by about 90 m3 from the figure in the ballast records and the approved BWM Plan.
f: Cross-check key figures across certificates and approved plans and ask class to correct errors.

t: Interviewee had not spotted the ballast capacity mismatch between the BWM certificate, the ballast records and the approved BWM Plan.
f: Check certificate data against approved plans whenever certificates are issued or renewed.

t: HVPQ had several errors: ship type as 'Other', wrong CII verification, owner ID number, survey date and P/V settings, and isolation valves wrongly declared.
f: Check HVPQ entries against certificates and nameplates, and leave non-applicable follow-ups blank.

t: The engine room fire contingency checklist did not include stopping ventilation fans and did not name the fixed systems on board, such as water mist.
f: Know the engine room fire checklist and check it covers stopping ventilation and every fixed system.

t: Emergency switchboard frequency and voltage meters lacked clear minimum marks, and the engineer opened a live cabinet to load the generator instead of using the switch.
f: Load the emergency generator with the proper control switch and keep meter limit marks clear.

t: The PMS told crew to refer to the AED maker's manual for testing and maintenance, but the manual was not on board; it was obtained later.
f: Keep maker manuals on board for every item the PMS refers to.

t: The operator had no procedure on what to do if a BNWAS stage 2 or 3 alarm sounded.
f: Know who responds to BNWAS stage 2 and 3 alarms and what they must do.

t: Drill reports did not show who took part, and the procedures did not require participants' names or ranks to be recorded.
f: Record the names and ranks of drill participants so anyone who missed it can catch up.

t: An interviewee did not know where the Emergency Towing Booklet was kept.
f: Know where the ship-specific Emergency Towing Booklet is kept and what it contains.

t: There was no requirement to test and record the electrical continuity of the flexible hoses kept for inerting double hull tanks.
f: Test and record electrical continuity of inerting hoses as you would for cargo hoses.

t: Two accommodation fire doors had puncture damage to the outer skin on one side.
f: Report damaged fire doors promptly, as damage can compromise their fire integrity.

t: Interviewee had not identified the damaged fire doors or taken any corrective action.
f: Check fire door panels, seals and closers during safety rounds.

t: Metal supports of the ducted rudder flaps on both lifeboats were heavily corroded.
f: Inspect lifeboat rudder and propeller fittings during LSA checks and treat corrosion early.

t: The corroded lifeboat rudder supports had been missed, and the safety inspection records did not match the condition found.
f: Make sure inspection records describe what you actually saw, not a copy of last month's.

t: The operator's entry procedures and permit form were not in line with the latest IMO recommendations, MSC.581(110).
f: Compare your permit with MSC.581(110) and report gaps to the office.

t: The metal stoppers limiting movement of the aft mooring winch control levers had corroded away and no longer worked.
f: Check winch control lever stops and guards are intact, and repair them before mooring.

t: A cargo pump hydraulic supply line on deck was leaking at a connection, leaving an oil patch of about 20 x 20 cm, and the line was badly corroded.
f: Watch hydraulic lines while cargo pumps run and stop and repair leaks at once.

t: The officer's deck inspection was not detailed enough and missed the winch lever stoppers and hydraulic line defects.
f: Inspect deck fittings and hydraulic lines closely; a walk-past inspection misses defects.

t: Visitor baggage was not searched as the company procedure required for the security level in force.
f: Search visitors' bags as the SSP requires for the current security level.

t: Also logged as a learning gap: visitor baggage searches required at the current security level were not carried out.
f: Practise gangway security routines, including baggage checks, in security drills.

t: The accompanying officer did not know the minimum anchor party make-up or that the maximum anchoring depth should be marked on the windlass or bridge.
f: Know your windlass's maximum anchoring depth and the minimum anchor party required.

t: Also logged as a learning gap: company anchoring procedures on anchor party size and maximum depth were not known.
f: Review the anchoring procedure before each anchorage and brief the anchor party.

t: The PMS set BWTS UV lamp replacement at five years, while the maker required replacement every 5,000 running hours.
f: Set PMS intervals to match maker requirements, by running hours where specified.

t: A stud in the starboard anchor cable was cracked and slightly dislodged, and it was not on the defect list.
f: Inspect anchor cable studs during anchoring and report any damage.

t: Interviewee was unfamiliar with the company defect reporting procedure.
f: Know how and where to report a defect in the company system.

t: Same gap logged as custom and practice: the interviewee did not know the company's defect reporting procedure.
f: Make reporting defects a habit, not something left to the C/O or C/E.

t: The HVPQ declared annual cargo line pressure tests at 24 bar, but the last annual test was at 16 bar.
f: Enter test pressures in the HVPQ from the actual test records.

t: Rest hour records showed rest split into three periods, some under one hour, although the ship's procedure claimed STCW compliance.
f: Rest may be split into no more than two periods, one at least 6 hours long; check entries daily.

t: Also logged as custom and practice: splitting rest into three short periods was routinely accepted in the rest hour records.
f: Plan work so rest comes in no more than two blocks, and flag non-compliant entries.

t: No role-specific familiarisation checklist existed for a specialist officer; the engineering checklist was used instead.
f: Use a familiarisation checklist matched to each role, including specialist officers.

t: Received VHF DSC messages were not recorded in the GMDSS log.
f: Log every DSC message received, including distress relays and tests.

t: The interviewee had not identified the cracked stud in the starboard anchor cable.
f: Check anchor cable links and studs closely during anchor inspections.

t: Interviewee was not familiar with the purpose or operation of the double block and bleed valve.
f: Know where double block and bleed valves are fitted and how to operate them.

t: Also logged as custom and practice: the function and operation of the double block and bleed valve were not understood.
f: Include double block and bleed valves in cargo system familiarisation.

t: Interviewee could not find the thermal protective aids in the rescue boat or explain their purpose, and was visibly very nervous during the interview.
f: Know where the TPAs are in each survival craft and what they are for; practise explaining LSA calmly.

t: Procedures covered daily and pre-arrival whistle tests, but not scheduled testing of the whistle's automatic signalling system.
f: Test the whistle's automatic fog signal function as well as the manual whistle.

t: Procedures did not define how competency assessments were done, which methods to use, or what training should follow identified gaps.
f: Know how your competency is assessed and keep evidence of training done to close any gaps.

t: Entry procedures gave no guidance on CO2 exposure limits, interpreting CO2 readings, or what to do when limits were exceeded.
f: Know the CO2 limits for safe entry and the action to take if readings exceed them.

t: A condition of class required the malfunctioning BWTS to be repaired within about six weeks.
f: Track class condition deadlines and push for technician attendance in time.

t: A conditional Ballast Water Management certificate, valid for about a month, had been issued because of the BWTS failure.
f: Know the expiry and conditions of any conditional certificate and what is needed to clear it.

t: The sound-powered telephone at the main engine local control position did not work when tested.
f: Test sound-powered telephones to every station regularly, including the engine local control.

t: The faulty sound-powered telephone at the engine local control position had not been reported in the defect system.
f: Report communication equipment failures as soon as they are found.

t: The HVPQ had wrong dates for the next in-water survey, last annual survey and last dry dock, a wrong SEC issue date and wrong heating data for one tank.
f: Update HVPQ survey and certificate dates whenever class or flag issue new documents.

t: No procedure existed for carrying out the periodic tests required by the manufacturer's instructions for navigation equipment.
f: Transfer maker-required periodic tests for bridge equipment into the PMS.

t: There was no procedure for marking escape routes from the bow thruster room, or from the accommodation to the shore access.
f: Check escape routes are clearly marked from every space, including the bow thruster room.

t: The BWTS failure was also logged under pollution prevention, with a class deadline to repair it within about six weeks.
f: Keep ballast water contingency measures in place while the BWTS is under a class condition.

t: There were no company procedures for inspecting and maintaining the electrical bonding on cargo pipelines.
f: Include cargo pipeline bonding straps in the PMS and check them during deck inspections.

t: The same sound-powered telephone fault at the engine local control position was also logged under machinery spaces.
f: Test emergency communications from the engine local control position during engine room checks.

t: Asked about loss of propulsion, the interviewee could not find the emergency plan in the ECR or show familiarity with the response.
f: Know where the loss-of-propulsion plan is kept and your role in it.

t: No personal or portable gas meter on board could measure CO2, although the meters covered O2, CO, H2S and HC.
f: Raise an early requisition for CO2-capable detectors if your ship has none.

t: Neither the enclosed space entry procedure nor the permit had been updated to the revised IMO recommendations, MSC.581(110).
f: Check the permit form version against the latest IMO guidance during SMS reviews.

t: The port side gyro compass repeater was not working; records showed it had worked before arrival.
f: Check all gyro repeaters, including on the bridge wings, during pre-arrival tests.

t: Interviewee could not explain hazardous energy types, the isolation steps or how to prove zero energy, despite recent training.
f: Know your LOTO steps: identify energy sources, isolate, lock, tag and prove zero energy.

t: Three poop deck scupper plugs were loose; deck rounds were said to be every 4 hours, but the SSSCL repetitive checks were not being used.
f: Use the SSSCL repetitive checks on every round and physically check scupper plugs.

t: HVPQ errors included the nitrogen buffer tank capacity given in m3/h, an old medical guide edition, and an incorrect winch brake holding load.
f: Check units and figures in the HVPQ against equipment data and publications on board.

t: Interviewee knew the foam monitors and hoses but could not find the portable foam applicator or explain its use, though familiarisation was recorded.
f: Know where the portable foam applicator is stowed and how to rig it for a deck fire.

t: The company gave no guidance on handling and disposing of the liquid used to pressure test the bunker line, or on recording its disposal.
f: Record how bunker line test liquid is drained and where it goes.

t: Interviewee could not explain how test fuel was drained from the lower athwartship bunker line section, and no records showed its disposal.
f: Know how every section of the bunker line is drained after testing, and keep a record.

t: Interviewee could not say where the ship's Emergency Towing Booklet was kept until checking it at the closing meeting.
f: Know where every copy of the Emergency Towing Booklet is kept on board.

t: The test handle of a relief valve on an HFO bunker line was seized by corrosion; it was freed and the valve worked before the inspection ended.
f: Exercise relief valve test handles during PMS checks so they do not seize.

t: Interviewee had not noticed the seized test handle on the bunker line relief valve.
f: Try test handles and moving parts during inspections rather than just looking at them.

t: A fall arrestor at the accommodation ladder was attached to a handrail, which was not a suitable anchor point.
f: Attach fall arrest gear only to rated anchor points, never to handrails.

t: Interviewee described the aft emergency towing method wrongly, not knowing the ship had a towing wire to connect to the tug's line.
f: Study the Emergency Towing Booklet and walk through deploying the towing gear at the station.

t: The procedure required ECDIS guard zones of 0.5 nm (coastal) and 2 nm (open sea), but the units fitted could only be set to 250 m.
f: Check procedure settings are achievable on your ECDIS model and report conflicts to the office.

t: Procedure required two-person engine watches in open sea daylight, but the engine room was left unmanned at lunch and after 17:00.
f: Run engine room watch levels as the procedure states, or get the procedure formally changed.

t: Flooding drills were due six-monthly, but the last pump room flooding drill was over a year earlier and only one of four scenarios was done each cycle.
f: Rotate all flooding scenarios through the drill plan so none goes unpractised.

t: The port pilot ladder had a cracked rubber step near the bottom and a partly broken step fixing piece below it.
f: Check each pilot ladder step and its fixings before use, and replace damaged ladders.

t: The officer had overlooked the cracked pilot ladder step and broken fixing piece during his safety inspection.
f: Inspect the full length of pilot ladders during safety rounds, not just the top section.

t: The fixed oxygen sensor near the inert gas fan was giving an erratic reading of 4.9% oxygen.
f: Calibrate IG oxygen analysers before use and cross-check them with a portable meter.

t: The bunker line pressure test procedure did not include testing the bunker system relief valve, and there was no evidence it had been tested.
f: Test bunker line relief valves along with the line pressure test and record the result.

t: No ship/shore cargo quantity comparisons were recorded at the last load port as SSSCL item 50 requires, and the form lacked a differences column.
f: Compare ship and shore figures at set intervals during cargo transfer and record the differences.

t: Interviewee could not explain or demonstrate the ECDIS date-dependent function, or how date-dependent manual objects are created and removed.
f: Practise creating date-dependent manual updates on ECDIS and know when they disappear.

t: Procedure required AIS on low power alongside during hydrocarbon discharge and banned switching it off, conflicting with ISGOTT guidance.
f: Know ISGOTT's options for AIS alongside a terminal and raise conflicting procedures with the office.

t: The self-igniting light on the pick-up rope buoy of the aft emergency towing gear did not work.
f: Test emergency towing buoy lights during routine checks of the towing arrangement.

t: Interviewee thought the towing buoy light only worked in darkness; tests showed a fault when the cover was tightened, and no repair was reported.
f: Test buoy lights in the dark (cover the sensor) and report any fault for repair.
